body.translated_text: <s>Tattvaratnāvalokaḥ</s> (The Illumination of the Jewel of Reality)
<s>Oṃ</s>! Homage to the feet of the glorious true teacher (<s>Sadguru</s>)!

children.translated_text: He who is of the form of incomparable bliss, <s>Śrīnivāsa</s> (Abode of Śrī), the shelterless one, who possesses the knowledge in the form of the ten incomparable Goddesses,

who brings about the attainment of happiness for the welfare of the three worlds, the changeless one — may <s>Kamalapāṇi</s> (the Lotus-Handed One) be victorious as long as the directions expand! (verse 1)
Those who do not know the form of the beautiful fourth empowerment (<s>caturtha-seka</s>) attained through the procedure of the glorious <s>mantra</s>, which is devoid of explicit words —
for their clear understanding, an effort is made with the seven divisions combined with groups of various instructions. (verse 2)

children.text: saṃbhrāntabodhā nikhilā hi tīrthyās tattvasya sādhyasya ca rūpavittau /
children.translated_text: For all the sectarians (<s>tīrthyas</s>) are confused in knowing the nature of reality (<s>tattva</s>) and of the goal (<s>sādhya</s>).

children.text: tebhyaḥ prakṛṣṭaḥ kila tattvavettā vedāntavādīti[jana] pravādaḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: Among them, the knower of <s>tattva</s> is said to be the highest — so goes the popular saying about the <s>Vedāntins</s>. (verse 3)
The <s>Vedāntins</s> declare the goal (<s>sādhya</s>) to be of the nature of bliss (<s>ānanda</s>), unshakeable by self-knowledge, peaceful;
and the <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> (Khaḍgas), and <s>Jains</s> desire the goal to be the cessation of the material conditions (<s>upadhi</s>) of form and the like. (verse 4)
Devoid of form, having the nature of the sky and moon, knowable by one's own self, and full of the essence of compassion,
adorned with the marks of existence, purposeful, issuing forth generosity (<s>dāna</s>) and the like, devoid of [worldly] happiness — (verse 5)
with body adorned by marks of bliss and existence, enjoyed by those abiding on the ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>),
those who follow the method of the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections) beginning with generosity declare the goal to be one that works for the benefit of beings. (verse 6)

children.text: saṃpūrya dānādiguṇānaśeṣān saṃbuddhya kṛtyaṃ sakalaṃ ca kṛtvā /
children.translated_text: Having fulfilled all qualities such as generosity, having fully awakened, and having accomplished all that is to be done,

children.text: yabhdūtakoṭeḥ karaṇaṃ ca sākṣāt sādhyaṃ tadapyasti nirodharūpam || 7 ||
children.translated_text: that which is the direct cause of the limit of existence (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>) — that goal too is of the nature of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>). (verse 7)
Embracing one's own consort, working for that purpose, of the nature of liberation from both suffering and happiness,
they declare the goal to be with body adorned by eighty minor marks (<s>anuvyañjana</s>), beyond conceptual elaboration (<s>kalpanā</s>). (verse 8)

children.text: svadevatākāraviśeṣaśūnyaṃ prāgeva saṃbhāvya sukhaṃ sphuṭaṃ sat /
children.translated_text: Devoid of the particular form of one's own deity, having previously established bliss as clear and real,
someone has declared [the goal] to be called <s>mahāsukha</s> (great bliss), working for the benefit of the world, resembling a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>). (verse 9)

children.text: kṛtvā sākṣāt svādhipaṃ sātarūpaṃ paścāt tyaktvā sātamātraṃ phalaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Having directly accomplished one's own lord (<s>svādhipa</s>) in the form of bliss,

children.text: śuddhaṃ sākṣācchakyate naiva kartuṃ tenākāro bhāvitaḥ svādhipasya || 10 ||
children.translated_text: afterward, having abandoned [that form], bliss alone would be the fruit. The pure [reality] cannot be directly accomplished; therefore the form of one's own lord is meditated upon. (verse 10)

children.text: gagaṇasamaśarīraṃ lakṣaṇairbhūṣitāṅgaṃ nirupamasukhapūrṇaṃ svābhayā saṃgataṃ ca /
children.translated_text: With a body like space, with limbs adorned by marks, full of incomparable bliss, united with one's own consort (<s>svābhā</s>),
a certain radiant, immeasurable lord of sages, working for the benefit of all beings, declares the goal to be free from annihilation (<s>uccheda</s>). (verse 11)

children.text: kṛtvā sākṣāt svādhipaṃ sātarūpaṃ bhāvopekṣājñānamātraṃ phalaṃ syāt /
children.translated_text: Having directly accomplished one's own lord in the form of bliss, the fruit would be mere knowledge of meditative equanimity (<s>bhāvopekṣā</s>).
Lasting as long as <s>saṃsāra</s>, working for the benefit of beings, resembling a wish-fulfilling jewel, absolutely peaceful. (verse 12)

children.text: kṛtvā sākṣānmaṇḍalaṃ sātarūpaṃ paścāttasya svecchayā nirvṛtiṃ ca /
children.translated_text: Having directly accomplished the <s>maṇḍala</s> in the form of bliss, and afterward its dissolution by one's own will —

children.text: sattvārthasyāpyastyabhāvo na vāsmin prādurbhāvo nirvṛtādasti yasmāt || 13 ||
children.translated_text: is there or is there not an absence of benefiting beings in this? Because there is manifestation [again] from dissolution. (verse 13)

children.text: kṛtvā sphuṭaṃ rūpamabhīṣṭameṣāṃ paścānnirodhaṃ phalamāha kaścit /
children.translated_text: Having clearly created the desired form of these [practitioners], someone says the fruit afterward is cessation (<s>nirodha</s>).

children.text: abhinnarūpaśca yato nirodho na pakṣabhede 'pi tato 'sti bhedaḥ || 14 ||
children.translated_text: And since cessation is of non-different form, therefore even in the difference of position there is no [real] difference. (verse 14)
After the knowledge of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), the tasting of <s>bodhicitta</s> — the fourth [empowerment] — [some say] the remaining empowerment is the highest,

children.text: yasmāt sarvo bhāvanāsu prayāso vyarthaḥ prāptastatphalasya prasiddheḥ || 15 ||
children.translated_text: since all effort in meditations (<s>bhāvanā</s>) is futile, because the attainment of its fruit is already well-established. (verse 15)
After the knowledge of <s>prajñā</s>, the tasting of the delight attained — the fourth empowerment is called the lowest [by others],

children.text: yasmāt sarvo bhāvanādau prayatno buddhoddiṣṭo niṣphalaḥ saṃprasaktaḥ || 16 ||
children.translated_text: since all effort in meditation and the like taught by the <s>Buddha</s> would [then] be attached and fruitless. (verse 16)
The <s>vajra</s>-seed, purified and cleansed by hearing (<s>śruti</s>), becoming a pure lotus-sprout, growing to nourishment —

children.text: turīyaśasyaṃ paripākameta(ti) sphuṭaṃ caturthaṃ viduṣo 'pi gūḍham || 17 ||
children.translated_text: the fourth crop (<s>turīya-śasya</s>) reaches full ripeness: the fourth [empowerment] is clear, yet hidden even from the wise. (verse 17)
The five lamps, drops of nectar, the moon, the <s>maṇḍalas</s> arising from the drop between the eyebrows,
the nature of the wind (<s>vāyu</s>), the uvula (<s>galaśuṇḍikā</s>) and so forth — these are not the true nature; one should investigate for oneself. (verse 18)
By [similes of] dream, magic (<s>indrajāla</s>), reflection (<s>pratibimba</s>), illusion (<s>māyā</s>), mirage (<s>marīci</s>), <s>gandharva</s>-city, and moon in water,
and by all other designated similes — the goal (<s>sādhya</s>) is nothing other than what has been stated here. (verse 19)

By words such as 'profound' (<s>gambhīra</s>), 'empty' (<s>śūnya</s>), 'mere appearance' (<s>pratibhāsamātra</s>), 'peaceful' (<s>śānta</s>), 'extremely subtle' (<s>atisūkṣma</s>), 'inexpressible' (<s>anabhilāpya</s>),
'unstained' (<s>nirlepa</s>), 'formless' (<s>nīrūpa</s>), 'untainted' (<s>nirañjana</s>), and the like — confusion should not be created regarding the reality of the other goal. (verse 20)

body.translated_text: This is the composition of the venerable Paṇḍita <s>Vāgīśvarakīrti</s>.
